first.rationale: Onboarding completion is down 4% and activation is also weakening, so simplifying onboarding addresses the clearest current funnel constraint while building on prior evidence that shorter onboarding and fewer signup fields improved time-to-value and SMB activation. I would run a guarded test with stop conditions tied to qualified pipeline, activation quality, and retention—not completion alone—to avoid optimizing shallow conversions. Promotional pricing may counter competitor pressure, but it risks margin and is less directly connected to the simultaneous onboarding decline.

final.rationale: Run a standard experiment shortening onboarding to address the current 4% completion decline and support the 6% activation decline. The verified record shows a 13% completion lift, 2.1-day faster time-to-value, and 3% higher 30-day retention, making this the strongest sustainable qualified-revenue opportunity. Use qualified activation, pipeline/revenue quality, and 30-day retention as success criteria, with a stop rule if downstream value deteriorates. The signup simplification evidence is SMB-specific and included a 1% retention decline, so it should not be broadly applied this week.
